chords._schema: strings ordered low E (6) to high e (1). frets: null = muted/not played, 0 = open. fingers: 0 = open, 1 = index, 2 = middle, 3 = ring, 4 = pinky, null = muted.

easyC.name: C major (Lauren's 'easy C' — 2-finger reduction)
easyC.note: Reduced 2-finger C voicing for confidence-building. Spelling verified deterministically by chord-theory-check.js (2026-08-08) as C E G. 'Lauren's easy C' is a teaching label; arithmetic proves the fingering spells C major and is playable.

pivot_points.static_finger: middle(2) stays on D-string 2nd fret in both shapes
pivot_points.movement: ring(3) moves A 2nd->3rd; nothing else moves. One finger relocates.

exercises.name: Find the anchor
exercises.purpose: Notice the shared finger between Em and easy C.

params.action: form Em, then easyC, watch the shared finger stay

exercises.coaching: In Em your middle finger is on the D string second fret. In easy C it is STILL there. That finger never moves — it is your anchor. Let it guide the change.

exercises.name: Air changes
exercises.purpose: Lift, move, land together — no guitar needed.

params.action: make shape in air, lift all, land all simultaneously

exercises.coaching: Lift your hand off the neck, make the next shape in the air, drop it down all at once. Landing together is faster than placing finger by finger.

exercises.name: 1-minute change drill
exercises.purpose: Count completed Em↔easyC changes in 60 seconds.
exercises.coaching: Metronome on, one minute: Em to easy C, back and forth, as many clean changes as you can. Count them. Write it down — that is next week's target.

avatar_coaching_copy.intro: The pause between chords is what makes beginners sound like beginners. Today we kill the pause with anchor fingers.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex1_intro: Your middle finger sits on the D string second fret in BOTH Em and easy C. It never moves. Anchor on it — the rest of the hand follows.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex2_intro: Air changes: lift off, shape the next chord in the air, drop it down all at once. Landing together beats placing finger by finger.
avatar_coaching_copy.ex3_intro: One minute, count your Em-easyC changes. Write the number. Next week, beat it by one. That is how slow becomes fast.
avatar_coaching_copy.results: A higher change-count than last week means your hands are learning. That is the only metric that matters here.
avatar_coaching_copy.wrap: Anchor fingers + air changes = faster switches. You just met your first measurable skill. Lesson 6 we add G.
